newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP to spend A$500 mln on coal expansion.
newsitem.headline: BHP to spend A$500 mln on coal expansion.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Thursday that it and its Central Queensland Coal Associates joint venture partners plan to spend A$500 million on the expansion of the Peak Downs and Saraji open-cut coking coal mines and the port of Hays Point.

The Peak Downs expansion would increase annual production by about three million tonnes in the year 2001/2 to 10 million tonnes, with a new large dragline as well as additional stripping, hauling and processing capacity.

BHP said Saraji's annual production would increase by about two million tonnes a year to about seven million tonnes in the year 2000. This expansion would also require additional stripping, hauling, processing and associated capacity.
It said throughput capacity expansion at Hay Point which began in 1996 would increase annual shipping capacity to more than 28 million tonnes in early 1998 from 24 million tonnes.
BHP has a 47.62 percent stake in the CQCA joint venture, which is managed by BHP Coal.
Other shareholders are QCT Resources Ltd with 29.58 percent, Mitsubishi Development with 14.19 percent and Australian life office AMP Society with 8.61 percent.
QCT said in a separate statement that the actual amount to be spent would be A$470 million, with its pro-rata expenditure being A$139 million.

"The expansion plans are part of a major review by BHP Coal of its coal interests in Australia and Indonesia, which aims to identify those properties with the greatest potential for future growth and earnings," BHP said.
"A range of cost and production improvements is also currently being undertaken by BHP Coal, which will result in increased and sustainable returns," it said.

BHP said Peak Downs and Saraji have extensive reserves of high quality coking coal which was exported to steel producers around the world. It said BHP-operated mines in central Queensland accounted for about 20 percent of the world's total seaborne trade in coking coal.

Approval of the expansion plans followed an agreement with the Queensland state government and Queensland Rail on freight package deal for five mines in the northern Bowen Basin, effective June 1 this year.
"These arrangements provide BHP and its joint venturers with long term planning stability and overall cost reductions, which have facilitated the expansion of the mining operations," BHP said.
